items.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: So that was real sad to see Billie Holiday only as a maid... listening to Billie Holiday at the beginning of her career and at the end of her career

ctx.x: I was interested in your comment when you said in order to get Basie in Hollywood we had to see some of the kind of bad Hollywood too. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

Well that’s particularly true for African American musicians who didn’t get the opportunity that white musicians got in the early part of the Hollywood history. So when we got jazz, that was one thing on film, it was another thing when we got African American jazz on film. And you see some of our great American musicians relegated to the roles that not only Hollywood placed on them, but all of America placed on them. So that was real sad to see Billie Holiday only as a maid, and Louis Armstrong only as a butler,…
I’ve read some really questionable things about a couple of filmings where if there was a white musician in the band they had to blacken his skin or vice versa.
